South Kaibab Trail itself remains open from the trailhead to Black Bridge, but Phantom Ranch is closed, so do not plan to reach it today; conditions could change quickly given the active flood watch. This trail is fully sun-exposed with no water source below the trailhead; water was on at the South Kaibab Trailhead as of the most recent check. Source: National Weather Service; National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon Country today; the prior warning expired Friday, August 28 at 8pm MST and was not renewed (Source: National Weather Service). Bright Angel Trail remains open from the trailhead to the River Resthouse; the status of the River Trail and Silver Bridge beyond that point could not be confirmed today given the flood closure, so hikers should not plan to continue past River Resthouse and should confirm current signage before descending further. Grand Canyon National Park advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk regardless of warning status. Water was on at the Bright Angel Trailhead and Havasupai Gardens as of the most recent check, but water status can change suddenly, so verify current conditions before descending. Source: National Weather Service; National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: North Kaibab Trail and Phantom Ranch are closed until further notice after a flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on the afternoon of August 29, 2026 required the National Park Service to conduct an aerial evacuation of roughly 50 people from the Phantom Ranch area; no injuries were reported. This closure is separate from, and precedes, a planned closure between Redwall Bridge and the north end of Cottonwood Campground beginning around October 15, 2026 for the Transcanyon Waterline Project, which is not yet in effect. The National Park Service continues to advise increased caution near Supai Tunnel and the lower trail due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and flash flooding with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead; this is especially relevant given the active Flood Watch for Grand Canyon Country through midnight Monday. Water status at the North Kaibab Trailhead, Supai Tunnel, and Cottonwood Campground should be considered uncertain until the National Park Service posts a post-flood update. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon Country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service; news reports of the August 29 evacuation.
